about: Nilai v4, a walk through the graph: 13 chapters, one per concept category. Each walks three corpus verses joined by two graded sound links and ends in one beat labelled imagined. Tamil lines, readings, flags and link texts are copied verbatim from kg/ by chapters_curate.py; validate_chapters.py checks them.

verses.label: Purananuru 6
verses.reading: Karikizhar wishes the Pandya Mudukudumi, whose form and fame reach from beyond the Himalaya to below Kumari, from sea to sea and from the waters below to the world above, that he may lean to no side like the beam of a balance, that his umbrella bow only in circling the three-eyed god's shrine, his head only before the raised hands of the Vedic sages, his garland wilt only in the smoke of burned enemy lands and his anger yield only to his women's sulking faces, and that he abide on earth like the cool moon and the burning sun.
verses.object: the beam of a balance (தெரிகோல் ஞமன்)
verses.asset_is: hand-held tharasu, a brass two-pan balance

verses.label: Maduraikkanchi (Pattuppattu 6), lines 489–506
verses.reading: Then the court that speaks right, which puts away fear, grief and desire, and keeps from both hatred and delight, being straight like the beam of a balance; the kaviti officers with sandal on their chests, who like the great ones who move in the sky examine good and evil and restrain them, keep love and right, shun blame and are full of fame; and the merchants who never stray from right, in many-roomed houses like a cluster of hills where kites perch and fly, rich with goods and food, selling things of hill, land and water and gems, pearls and gold from excellent countries.
verses.object: the beam of a balance (ஞெமன்கோல்), the court likened to it
verses.asset_is: hand-held tharasu, a brass two-pan balance

verses.label: Tirukkural 118
verses.reading: To be settled and lean to no side, like the balance that first makes itself level and then weighs, is the ornament of the worthy.
verses.object: the balance that first levels itself, then weighs (சமன்செய்து சீர்தூக்குங் கோல்)
verses.asset_is: hand-held tharasu, a brass two-pan balance

links.text: The impartiality that the earlier poem asks of the king in person has, in Nedunjeliyan's Madurai, become the work of an institution, and the idyll spells out the five passions the court must set aside, which the wish to the king left unnamed.

true_direction.reads: pattupattu:6:489-506 develops purananuru:6

links.text: The idyll's list says what the Kural's 'first making itself level' consists of, the clearing of five named passions before judgment, so the couplet's compressed image can be unpacked from a description of a working court.

true_direction.reads: pattupattu:6:489-506 develops kural:118

forward.text: The balance passed from a king’s person to a court, and the Kural asked it to level itself before it weighs. In 2526 machines do the weighing; we ask who levels them first.
forward.label: கற்பனை · imagined

then.asset_is: hand-held tharasu, a brass two-pan balance

forward.transformation: the brass tharasu becomes the sealed laboratory balance

chapters.subtitle: the parasol, and who falls outside its shade

verses.label: Purananuru 35

links.text: The Kural ties rain to the king's public justice only, while the Kalittokai grants the rain and still finds injustice at home, so the friend shows that the doctrine's measure of a ruler can be met in full while a wife is wronged.

links.text: The Naladiyar says the body appears like mist on a hill and goes, so its owners should take the fruit it can yield while they have it (யாக்கையால் ஆய பயன்கொள்க). நோய்க லந்த வாழ்வு றாமல் நீக லந்து ளாகு ஞான

verses.reading: The poet speaks of the body of four and five gates, a bush of sinew and bone with arms and legs, in which sound joins at the first gate and its plays go on unnoticed, and asks that before it grows old in seeking endless books and speaking clever words to men he be given a life of reciting fully the books of knowledge in which Murugan is mingled. The praise names the primal one who cried 'refuge' when Death came casting his noose for the boy's life, the silent dark-throated one who looked at Kama and his five arrows and said 'burn', to whom Murugan spoke the Veda, and Vishnu with the discus who ended the elephant's fear, at Senthil where the Vedas seek the feet.
verses.object: endless crores of books (நூல் அனந்த கோடி)

verses.label: Naladiyar 135
verses.reading: Learning has no shore, learners have few days, and, thought over calmly, many illnesses; so the wise learn with clear discernment what is fitting, like the bird that drinks the milk and leaves the water.

verses.image_note: குருகு is a heron or crane; 10-H is a pond heron (no milk bowl in the image)

verses.label: Tirumanthiram 2720
verses.reading: Though one recites the Vedas with their limbs and the Agamas, what is ours lies in one letter of our Lord; master that one letter with doubt destroyed and one becomes a precious vessel that has reached the farther shore.
verses.object: the precious vessel that reaches the farther shore (அங்கரை சேர்ந்த அருங்கலம்)

links.text: The Naladiyar says learning has no shore and the learner's days are few, so one should choose what is fit, like the bird drinking the milk from the water. 70 asks that before the body ages in seeking endless crores of books (நூல் அனந்த கோடி தேடி) he be given the books of knowledge in which the Lord is mingled (நீ கலந்துள ஞான நூல்). Both set limited life against unlimited books; 70 names the choice as the jnana books.

links.text: Both answer endless learning with a choice: the Naladiyar says learning has no shore and life is short, so take only what is fitting, as the swan takes milk from water; Tirumular names the one thing to take, the Lord's letter, and makes it the vessel that does reach the shore.
